newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Party names Sharif for Pakistan prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Party names Sharif for Pakistan prime minister.

text.p: The party that won a landslide in Pakistans general elections on February 3 named its leader Nawaz Sharif on Friday to be prime minister for the second time, succeeding his rival, ousted Benazir Bhutto.
The parliamentary groups of Sharifs main Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party and its smaller allies unanimously elected him as their parliamentary leader.
That position automatically makes him their prime ministerial candidate.

Sharif, 47, is certain to be elected to the office on Monday by the 217-seat National Assembly (lower house), where the PML and its allies have a more than two-thirds majority won in the elections, in which Bhuttos Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) suffered a crushing defeat.
About 150 newly-elected deputies attended Fridays meeting at a hotel and greeted Sharifs election with loud cheers, witnesses said.

Bhutto accuses President Farooq Leghari and a caretaker government he installed after sacking her in November of rigging the elections, but says she will not launch protests for the sake of Pakistans stability. The government rejects the charge.
Sharif first became prime minister in 1990, after winning an election that also followed a dismissal of Bhuttos government by then president Ghulam Ishaq Khan on disputed corruption charges.

His government was dismissed by Ishaq two and half years later on similar charges, but was restored 35 days later by the Supreme Court, which held the presidential action under a controversial constitutional provision to be illegal.
Sharif and Ishaq Khan both resigned later in an army-brokered deal for a fresh election, which Bhutto won.
Last month, the Supreme Court rejected Bhuttos plea for a restoration of her government in the same way it did with Sharif and upheld the presidential action, as it did in 1990.
As the PML met to name Sharif for prime minister, Bhutto met her own party deputies to decide whether to sit in the new National Assembly or boycott it.

At a meeting on Thursday in the Punjab provincial capital of Lahore, many of the PPPs losing candidates accused the army of rigging the February 3 elections, when about 250,000 troops were deployed across the country to help civilian authorities maintain the peace during polling.
